feed.title: Jim Cramer Suggests Against Holding Dominion (D) Through the NextEra (NEE) Share Conversion
feed.summary: Jim Cramer advises Dominion Energy (D) shareholders to "take the money and run" rather than holding their shares through the upcoming conversion into NextEra Energy (NEE) stock if the merger is approved. The article details the $67 billion all-stock transaction forming the world's largest regulated utility, while also addressing regulatory scrutiny, high balance sheet leverage for both companies, and institutional positioning.

feed.title: Could ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) Be Entering A New Oil Cycle?
feed.summary: The article discusses ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) within the context of a new oil cycle, focusing on production discipline and portfolio integration. It highlights how the company's operational execution, genuine demand strength, and ability to adapt to changing market conditions are more crucial than short-term market sentiment. The analysis emphasizes the importance of clear communication, durable demand, and execution discipline for ConocoPhillips to succeed in the evolving oil and gas landscape amidst broader market shifts.

feed.title: Equinix Sees AI Driving Data Center Demand, Interconnection Growth
feed.summary: Equinix executives indicate that artificial intelligence is significantly accelerating demand for high-density data center capacity and interconnection services, requiring more complex, low-latency infrastructure. The company's interconnection business grew 9% this year, supported by new offerings like Fabric One and Inference Exchange, which address the complex networking needs of AI workloads. Equinix anticipates 9%-12% annual adjusted funds from operations per-share growth through 2029, driven by robust demand and development projects generating mid-20% cash yields.

feed.title: Kroger Has More Leverage Over Premium Brands. Now Boar’s Head and Red Bull Are Losing Shelf Space
feed.summary: Kroger is removing premium brands like Boar’s Head and Red Bull from some of its stores as part of a new strategy to lower prices and gain leverage over suppliers. CEO Greg Foran aims to reinvest savings from more efficient operations and sourcing into making the retailer more affordable to compete with other major grocers. While Boar's Head confirmed its products are still available in many Kroger locations and other retailers, the move signals a shift in Kroger's merchandising strategy.

feed.title: Agilent (A) Wants Pathology Labs To Go Digital, 540 Slides At A Time
feed.summary: Agilent Technologies (A) has launched a new slide scanner, the Agilent S540MD, in the U.S., capable of holding 540 glass slides. This FDA-cleared device aims to help pathology labs digitize their workflows and prepare for AI assistance, leveraging Agilent's expertise despite the underlying hardware being from Hamamatsu. The launch follows a strong financial quarter for Agilent, though the full impact of the scanner on revenue remains to be seen.

feed.title: Enterprise security shifts to the data layer at Oracle
feed.summary: Oracle is repositioning enterprise security to focus on the data layer, addressing new risks introduced by AI. The company's strategy involves securing data at the source, at speed, and through resilience, emphasizing robust security controls where data resides. This approach is built on a "shared accountability model" and will be a key discussion point at Oracle's upcoming virtual event, "AI Cyberattacks Are Escalating: How to Secure Your Data Now."

feed.title: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to meet on Sunday at JPMorgan headquarters
feed.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are scheduled to meet on Sunday at JPMorgan Chase headquarters in New York. The meeting will address AI security, trade, and other economic matters, occurring just days before President Donald Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. feed.title: Salesforce after Dreamforce: How the CRM giant can grow beyond its own interface
feed.summary: Salesforce's future growth hinges on AI agents doing more work outside its traditional interface, transforming customer interaction from application screens to desired outcomes. The company is developing an enterprise AI harness, combining data, business knowledge, workflows, and controls, to integrate deterministic software with large language models. This approach, supported by customer interest in "Agentforce" and "Headless" access, aims to position Salesforce as the essential system for making AI useful to businesses, extending its reach beyond its own UI and potentially increasing consumption on its platform.

feed.title: KeyCorp Reaffirms 2026 Outlook as Loan Growth, Margins and Fees Gain Momentum

The bank raised its fee-income growth outlook to 4-5% following the Clearwater acquisition and is increasingly confident in achieving a core return on tangible common equity of over 15% by 2027. feed.title: NASDAQ: ASTS: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Announces
feed.summary: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP has announced the filing of a securities fraud class action lawsuit against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ: ASTS). The lawsuit alleges that AST made materially false and misleading statements regarding its capital position, competitive durability, and user adoption between March 4, 2025, and July 15, 2026. Investors who purchased ASTS securities during this period and suffered losses are encouraged to contact the law firm to seek lead plaintiff status by November 13, 2026.

feed.title: Costco brings back a fan-favorite food court treat after years off the menu
feed.summary: Costco has announced the limited-time return of its twisted churro to U.S. food courts, much to the delight of fans who have been requesting its comeback for two years. The announcement followed a cryptic social media tease from the company, sparking widespread speculation among shoppers. While many celebrated the churro's return at its original price of $1.49, some expressed disappointment that it was only for a limited time or that it wasn't the older, classic straight version.

feed.title: Cencora (COR) Raised Guidance and Bought Back $1B. What’s the Catch?
feed.summary: Cencora (COR) reported strong fiscal third-quarter results, with revenue up 5.1% and adjusted EPS climbing 12.0%, leading to raised full-year guidance and $1 billion in stock repurchases. However, this profit growth significantly outpaced sales growth, driven by the OneOncology acquisition which also introduced higher operating expenses and debt. The article highlights a key tension: while profit margins improved due to the acquisition, the long-term sustainability is questioned by increased costs, interest expenses, and the rising volume of lower-margin GLP-1 drugs.

feed.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger helped protect 240,000 acres of California ranchland; the vast habitat is home to rare species and condors
feed.summary: Former California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger played a significant role in the landmark 2008 agreement that protected up to 240,000 acres of the 270,000-acre Tejon Ranch. This vast ranchland, located at the confluence of four ecological regions, is crucial habitat for the California condor and over 60 other at-risk plant and animal species. While Schwarzenegger publicly announced the deal, the negotiations were primarily conducted between the Tejon Ranch Company and five major environmental organizations, establishing a long-term conservation and land-use framework.

feed.title: Luck Stone Builds on Autonomous Hauling Success with Caterpillar
feed.summary: Luck Stone is expanding its autonomous hauling technology, in collaboration with Caterpillar, to two additional Virginia quarries following a successful 18-month pilot at Bull Run Quarry. The expansion, which will integrate Caterpillar’s autonomous hauling technology on Cat 775 trucks, aims to enhance safety, improve production consistency, and create new skill development opportunities for associates. This marks a significant milestone as it's the first deployment of this specific autonomous solution on the Cat 775 model, further contributing to Caterpillar's growing success in quarry autonomy.

feed.title: Bank of America Sets 12-Month S&P 500 Target at 7,800, Sees 2% Upside
feed.summary: Bank of America (BofA) has set a 12-month S&P 500 target of 7,800, representing a 2% upside from current levels, while also raising its year-end forecast to 7,400. Strategist Savita Subramanian highlighted potential market risks including inflation, Federal Reserve policy, and credit conditions, noting that half of BofA's bear market indicators have been triggered. Despite near-term concerns, BofA maintains a positive long-term outlook for equities, projecting significant earnings growth for the S&P 500 in 2026 and 2027, and favoring large-cap value stocks and equal-weighted indexes.

feed.title: The Discontinued Campbell's Canned Soup Flavor That Left A Hole In Some Holiday Traditions
feed.summary: Campbell's has discontinued its cream of shrimp soup, disappointing many home cooks who relied on it for holiday recipes like shrimp dip and casserole. The soup, which reportedly disappeared from shelves in 2025, is no longer listed on the company's website. For those looking to recreate the flavor, alternatives include using Blue Runner's cream of shrimp soup, doctoring Campbell's cream of onion soup with shrimp and tomato puree, or making a scratch-made version.

feed.title: Amgen or Merck: Which Drugmaker Has the Stronger Dividend Growth Story?
feed.summary: This article compares Amgen (AMGN) and Merck (MRK) as dividend growth investments, concluding that Amgen offers a stronger dividend growth story. Amgen provides a higher current yield, more consistent and aggressive dividend raises, and a more diversified product portfolio, making its dividend more durable against future patent expirations. Merck, while having growth potential, relies heavily on its Keytruda franchise and faces challenges with its pipeline execution.
